localBiteReport: The most detailed on-the-water reports for Choctawhatchee Bay are roughly two weeks old as of this writing. Capt. Blake Nelson (Last Cast Charters) reported in late October that the redfish bite on the bay's flats remained productive despite recent storm effects, with fish in the 23-inch-and-under range holding in guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas; he noted they were keying on small shrimp, crabs, and worms, making subtle bottom presentations like a Ned rig effective. A FishingBooker angler report from about a week ago mentioned landing two solid redfish while also picking up bait and fishing under the bridge. Water temperature at this location is 74°F. Sheepshead are typical this time of year around bridge pilings and jetties, and the cooler November temps historically signal an improving sheepshead bite along with speckled trout holding in deeper bayous and creek mouths — though no specific keeper-trout or flounder reports were confirmed this week. Note: Florida's inshore flounder season closes October 15 and does not reopen until December 1, so flounder should not be targeted in-bay right now.
